title: Viewer-bound leaderboard cursor v1
description: The record a leaderboard cursor carries, and the presentation it is evaluated against. The `Cursor` parameter of packages/schemas/openapi-v1.yaml already asserted that the server 'rejects a cursor it did not issue, a cursor issued against a different snapshot_id, and a cursor issued to a different principal'. Nothing in the repository held the fields those three refusals compare, so the sentence was a promise about an opaque string. A cursor names the generation it was issued against, the viewer it was issued to, the authorization revision that held at issue and the instant it stops being honoured; conformance/planning/ranking-cursor-vectors-v1.json states each way a presentation can fail and scripts/repository/validate_planning_artifacts.py evaluates the rules rather than reading the expected outcome back. docs/architecture/LEADERBOARD_STORAGE_AND_RANKING.md owns the access path the anchor serves.

generation.description: The sealed generation the anchor is an offset into. A cursor without it anchors a position in a table whose rows moved, which is how a page repeats an entry and skips another across a promotion.

snapshot_id.description: The durable client-visible name of that generation. It is carried as well as the generation because the client holds this one and never sees the integer.

position_after.description: The rank() position the next page starts after. Positions are frozen at seal, so the anchor stays valid while entries are suppressed from the rendered page: a page can be shorter than the limit while more entries remain.

authorization_revision.description: The revision of the audience's authorization inputs at issue. A presentation carrying a later revision is refused rather than served, because the alternative is replaying an authorization decision that has since changed — which is the case SR-015 names.

principal.description: Who the cursor was issued to. `anonymous` is admissible only for the global board, which is the one audience with no viewer; it is a named kind rather than an absent field, because an absent viewer and an anonymous viewer must not be the same value.
